Fitted a logistic regression (logit link) on the 80 records: Remission (PR=1 vs SD+PD=0) ~ Age + BMI + Gender. The change in log-odds of remission for each one-year increase in age is −0.0795 (≈ −0.08), holding BMI and gender constant.

Age (per +1 year): coefficient = −0.0795, SE = 0.0263, z = −3.02, p = 0.0025, 95% CI = [−0.131, −0.028]. Odds ratio = 0.924 (95% CI 0.877–0.972). So each additional year of age is associated with a statistically significant decrease in the log-odds (odds) of remission.

Full model (all three predictors, MLE, N=80, converged, pseudo-R²=0.124, LLR p=0.0033):
- Age:    coef −0.0795, SE 0.0263, z −3.02, p 0.0025, 95% CI [−0.131, −0.028], OR 0.924
- BMI:    coef  0.1621, SE 0.1088, z  1.49, p 0.136,  95% CI [−0.051,  0.375], OR 1.176 (not significant)
- Gender: coef −0.6132, SE 0.5471, z −1.12, p 0.262,  95% CI [−1.686,  0.459], OR 0.542 (not significant; Male=1 vs Female=0)
- (intercept 1.5313, SE 2.776, p 0.581)

Diagnostics: Hosmer–Lemeshow χ²=8.35, df=8, p=0.40 (good fit); predicted probabilities 0.12–0.90 (no separation).
